questions.question: For nonnegative loss $X$ and fixed strict franchise threshold $d>0$, payment is $X\mathbf1_{\{X>d\}}$. Does this rule make payment continuous as loss rises through the threshold?
options: Yes; qualifying payment is only the excess and starts continuously from zero.
No; payment jumps from zero to an amount just above the threshold.
Yes; all losses are paid in full, so their payments increase continuously.
No; payment falls from the whole loss to zero once the threshold is exceeded.

questions.question: A loss equals a threshold $d>0$. A strict franchise pays the whole loss only for $X>d$, while an inclusive franchise pays it for $X\ge d$. What are the payments under the strict and inclusive rules, respectively?
For nonnegative loss $X$ and strict franchise threshold $d>0$, payment is $Y=X\mathbf1_{\{X>d\}}$. Which interval excludes positive payments for every loss law under this rule?
Let $X\ge0$ have $\mathbb{P}(X>d)>0$ at strict franchise threshold $d\ge0$. Which identity for the positive-payment law holds for every such loss model and threshold?
The same nonnegative loss $X$ is subject either to strict franchise threshold $d\ge0$ or ordinary deductible $d$. Which comparison holds for every such loss law and threshold?
options: The franchise probability is larger because its payments are larger.
They are equal to $\mathbb{P}(X>d)$ under both rules.
The ordinary probability is larger because its payments are smaller.
They are equal to $\mathbb{P}(X\ge d)$ under both rules.

questions.question: At strict franchise threshold 60 euros, two ground-up losses are 50 euros and 90 euros. What are the respective insurer payments?
A loss equals 0, 40 or 100 euros with probabilities $0.2$, $0.5$ and $0.3$. A strict franchise threshold is 40 euros. What is the probability of positive payment?
A loss equals 10 euros with probability $0.6$ and 80 euros with probability $0.4$. Under strict franchise threshold 30 euros, what is expected payment per loss?
A loss equals 20, 60 or 100 euros with probabilities $1/2$, $1/4$ and $1/4$. With strict franchise threshold 40 euros, what is expected payment conditional on payment being positive?
For the same realised loss, a strict franchise threshold of 25 euros produces payment of 70 euros. What payment would an ordinary deductible of 25 euros produce?
For a nonnegative loss $X$, strict franchise threshold $d>0$ and payment $Y=X\mathbf1_{\{X>d\}}$, which formula gives $\mathbb{P}(Y\le y)$ for every loss law and every $0\le y\le d$?
Fix a realised nonnegative loss $x$ and strict franchise thresholds $0\le d_1<d_2$. Let $y_j=x\mathbf1_{\{x>d_j\}}$ for $j=1,2$. Which comparison must hold?

A strict franchise rule has loss $X\ge0$, threshold $d\ge0$ and payment $Y=X\mathbf1_{\{X>d\}}$. Monetary units are rescaled by $a>0$, so $X^*=aX$ and $d^*=ad$. Which formula for $Y^*$ holds for every such loss law and positive unit factor?
A loss $X$ has $\mathbb{P}(X>40)=0.5$ and $\mathbb{P}(X>80)=0.2$. With strict franchise threshold 40 euros, what is the probability a payment exceeds 80 euros, conditional on being positive?
At deductible $d=40$ euros, a nonnegative loss has positive-payment probability $0.3$ and ordinary-deductible expected payment 18 euros. What is expected payment under the strict franchise rule?
A loss $X$ is uniform on $[0,100]$ euros, with density $1/100$ on that interval. What is expected strict franchise payment at threshold 60 euros?

Two loss models use the same strict franchise threshold $d>0$ and have identical conditional positive-payment distributions with finite mean $m>0$. Does that alone force their expected payments per loss to be equal?
options: Yes; both per-loss means must equal m.
Yes; the common threshold forces equal qualifying frequencies.
No; their probabilities of qualifying may differ.
No; franchise payment subtracts d from the conditional mean.

questions.question: For a nonnegative loss $X$ and threshold $d>0$, compare strict franchise payment $Y_s=X\mathbf1_{\{X>d\}}$ with inclusive payment $Y_i=X\mathbf1_{\{X\ge d\}}$. When are their payment distributions identical?
options: Always, since equality is only one loss value.

questions.question: A loss equals 20, 50 and 100 euros with probabilities $0.2$, $0.3$ and $0.5$. Which full interval of strict franchise thresholds $d\ge0$ gives expected payment exactly 50 euros?

A nonnegative loss $X$ has strict franchise threshold 30 euros. Positive payment occurs with probability $1/2$ and mean payment per loss is 40 euros. What is the sharp range of possible ground-up means $\mathbb{E}[X]$ consistent with these observations?
